# @k8ordo/ui

> React components from k8ordo, with semantic design tokens, dark mode,
> built-in Japanese/English wording, AI chat components, and official generative UI
> adapters (json-render & OpenUI) that let an LLM generate, validate, and render
> on-brand UIs from these components.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses only
> what has reached Baseline, and ships no polyfills or legacy fallbacks — so
> nothing here branches for a browser or a framework it does not support.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.
Start with the Design Guide, then follow the reference most relevant to the task.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/GUIDE.md): setup, dark mode (the `dark` class that `@k8ordo/color-scheme` puts on `<html>`, and the `color-scheme` the stylesheet sets to match), i18n (default Japanese, switching to English), design direction, aesthetic guidelines, component usage principles, anti-patterns, implementation principles, testing (component tests belong in a real browser — Vitest browser mode or Playwright — because the components call browser APIs jsdom does not implement).

## References

- [Components](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/components.md): full component list, import paths, props, and i18n — every component, compound ones included (`Dialog.Root`, `Tabs.Root`, …), renders from a Server Component — component wording comes from a dictionary that defaults to Japanese; `@k8ordo/ui/i18n` exports `ja` / `en` / `dictionaries` (both keyed by locale) / the `Messages` type for `<UIProvider messages={...}>` (per-component wording props win over the dictionary), and `useMessages` to read the wording in effect in your own elements.
- [AI chat](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/ai-chat.md): AI chat components from `@k8ordo/ui/ai` (Conversation / Message / PromptInput / Reasoning / Suggestion / ToolInvocation), streaming Markdown `Response` from `@k8ordo/ui/ai/response` (optional peer `streamdown`), and `mapMessageParts` from `@k8ordo/ui/ai-sdk` to render AI SDK `UIMessage.parts` (optional peer `ai`).
- [Generative UI](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/generative-ui.md): use json-render / OpenUI to make an LLM generate UIs — `catalog.prompt()` (server-safe), `<JsonRenderUI spec={spec} />` (client), `validateGeneratedSpec()` (validate/repair LLM output), `satisfies UISpec` (typed specs), `@k8ordo/ui/openui/prompt`, and which exports the catalog leaves out on purpose.
- [Typography](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/typography.md): type scale and usage.
- [Color](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/color.md): semantic token system and dark mode.
- [Spacing & layout](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/spatial-design.md): spacing scale and layout patterns.
- [Interaction](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/interaction-design.md): motion and interaction guidelines.
- [Types](https://ordo.k8o.me/docs/references/types.md): the shared types for typing component props (`Status` / `Direction` / `Placement` / `ModalSide` / `DrawerSide` / `Option`).

## Data exports

- `@k8ordo/ui/tokens`: the design tokens resolved to JS values — `tokens` (`theme` / `vars` / `refs`), `meta`, and key unions such as `ColorToken`.
- `@k8ordo/ui/props.json`: every component's props as JSON (`docs/props.generated.json`), generated from the types — the same data as the Props blocks in components.md.

# @k8ordo/form

> Derive HTML constraint attributes, error messages, and server-side validation
> from one zod schema. The DOM holds the values; React state holds only what the
> DOM cannot express. Forms work with JavaScript disabled or not yet loaded.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses only
> what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or legacy
> fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/form/docs/GUIDE.md): the server/client split, writing a form end to end,
  what the package guarantees, what it does not do yet, and how it pairs with
  `@k8ordo/ui` without depending on it.

## Not supported

`z.array(z.file())` derives repeated single-file rows, not one `multiple` input.
Constraints behind a `.transform()` (or a `.pipe()` whose output JSON Schema
cannot describe) are not derived: the field becomes a bare text input and is
listed in `dropped`. There is no input masking. A schema no control could
satisfy is refused at derive time rather than left to fail on every
submission: `z.number()` and `z.literal(1)` (use `z.coerce.number()`),
`z.date()`, and `z.bigint()`; so is a `z.stringbool().default(true)` checkbox,
which could never submit `false`. A `z.custom()` that rejects strings cannot be refused at derive
time: it derives as a text input, is listed in `dropped`, and fails on the
server. Of `.refine()` / `.superRefine()` checks, `dropped` counts only the ones
on the schema as a whole, not those on a single field, a nested object, or a
row. Rules cannot target fields inside repeated rows.

## Entry points

- `@k8ordo/form` — client. `useForm(fields, state?)` takes the whole
  `formFields` result (and the action's state, when there is one) and
  returns props for the `<form>` element — which also hear a reset, React's
  own after every form action included — a
  `field(path)` accessor giving input attributes, the current error, and
  `invalid` / `required`, an `array(path)` accessor for repeated rows,
  `formError` (the message no field owns, with the props that let focus land
  on it), and `isDirty`. On submit it checks every field — untouched ones and
  the rules included — and stops a failing submission, a GET form with no
  action as much as one with (a `formNoValidate` button skips the check);
  after a submission stopped here or failed on the server, focus moves to the
  first failure in document order. Also `useAsyncCheck` for server-answered
  per-field checks and `HiddenValue` for components that render no input of
  their own. The types
  of the `formFields` result (`FormFields`, `DerivedField`, `DerivedArray`,
  `DroppedCheck`, `FieldInput`, `ValidityFlag`, `Rule`, `DerivedRule`,
  `RuleMessage`) are exported here as
  well, since the result crosses to the client as a prop, and so are
  `FormState` and the return types (`UseFormReturn`, `FieldView`, `ArrayView`,
  `RowView`, `FormErrorView`, `AsyncCheck`).
- `@k8ordo/form/server` — server. `formFields(schemaOrDefinition)` derives
  serializable fields plus a `dropped` list of checks HTML cannot express
  (outside production the list is also logged once per schema with
  `console.warn`), and throws on a schema no form can represent (including a
  leaf that could never accept a submitted string, such as `z.number()`);
  `parseForm(schemaOrDefinition, formData)` validates a submission and returns
  typed data or per-field errors with the submitted values. An untouched
  control reaches the schema as what it actually submits: `''` for text,
  `false` for a checkbox, and nothing at all for a number, a
  `z.coerce.bigint()`, a file, a choice (a radio group with none selected, a
  `<select>` on a `value=""` placeholder), or a `z.stringbool()` checkbox —
  which, checked, submits the `value` derived from the schema's own spelling of
  `true`, the same string `@k8ordo/state` writes into a URL — so `z.coerce.number()` cannot read a
  blank field as 0 and `z.enum([…]).optional()` can be left empty. A checkbox
  group always echoes as an array.
  `defineForm(schema, rules)` attaches cross-field rules (`sameAs`,
  `minChecked`, `requiredWhen`) typed against the schema's paths; a rule's
  message is a string or a function called when the rule is reported
  (`formFields` calls it while deriving, so a rule crosses to the client as a
  `DerivedRule` with the text in it; `parseForm` calls it when the rule
  breaks), which keeps a localized definition at module scope. Types:
  `ParseResult`, `FormDefinition`, `Rule`, `RuleMessage`, `FormState`, and the
  `formFields` result's `FormFields`, `DerivedField`, `DerivedArray`,
  `DerivedRule`, `DroppedCheck`, `FieldInput`, `ValidityFlag`.

# @k8ordo/state

> Declare state by where it lives: `definePageState` (typed URL search params
> plus hidden history-entry state — the two faces of one entry, updated
> atomically over the Navigation API), `defineLocalState` (localStorage,
> cross-tab), `defineMemoryState` (a typed shared box with no schema, resets
> on reload). One zod schema per boundary place (url, entry, local) derives
> the server read, canonical links, salvage of stale data, and a client
> subscription with exact per-key change detection. Links and GET forms write
> the URL before JavaScript loads under any router (the server renders what
> they wrote wherever it reads the search); imperative url updates ride a
> Navigation-API-intercepting router.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/state/docs/GUIDE.md): the four places and when each fits, the shared
  definition module, reading on the server, updating on the client, batching
  and update handles, subscription granularity, router requirements, typed
  routes via `Register`, reading local state before hydration, and pairing
  with `@k8ordo/form` for GET forms.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/state` — `definePageState(key, { url?, entry? })` returns a pure
  definition usable from server and client: `parseUrl(searchParams)` reads
  the url slot typed with defaults applied and invalid values salvaged
  (wherever the router hands a page its search — under `@k8ordo/static` /
  `@k8ordo/server` a page receives `params` and `pathname` (plus a
  headers-and-cookies `request` under `@k8ordo/server`) but never the search,
  and the url slot is read in the browser);
  `href(path, values?)` builds a canonical link keeping the path literal in
  the type — the path written from the app's root, the link carrying Vite's
  `base` (`import.meta.env.BASE_URL`) in front; `search(values?)` returns the
  query string alone.
  `defineLocalState(key, schema)` and `defineMemoryState(key, initial)`
  declare app-scope state; a local definition also exposes `storageKey` (the
  localStorage key, `k8ordo-state:<key>`) and `inlineRead()`, a JavaScript
  expression for an inline `<script>` that evaluates to the stored object or
  `null` before hydration — unvalidated, so read only what you need with a
  fallback. `useAppState(definition, keys?, { initialUrl? })`
  (client) works on any kind and returns `[state, update]` — state is the
  flat merge of a page definition's slots; `update(patch)` applies
  synchronously, batches the calls a handler makes with no `await` between
  them into one write (url+entry changes atomically via
  `navigation.navigate()`, entry-only changes via `updateCurrentEntry()`,
  local via one `setItem`; memory applies per call), and returns
  `{ committed, finished }` promise handles (for non-navigating kinds they
  settle once the write lands, and a write localStorage refuses rejects them
  with its error; `{ history: 'push' }` exists only on page state and takes
  effect only when a url value changes).
  `resetStateRegistry()` clears stores between tests. Augment
  `interface Register { routes: typeof routes }` — the same line as for
  `@k8ordo/router` — to check each `href` path against the route table's
  linkable patterns segment by segment (`NavigablePath`, so a `/:locale`
  table no longer takes every path); a router without a table registers its own path union as
  `interface Register { path }` instead.

---

# @k8ordo/router

> The URL's pathname axis, owned. One `defineRoutes` table is the application's
> pathname schema: types, matching, links and navigation all come from it, over
> the Navigation API and URLPattern. Search params and history-entry state are
> not its business — those belong to `@k8ordo/state`.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/router/docs/GUIDE.md): the table's grammar (leaves, branches, params,
  wildcards, route groups, declaration order), mounting `<Router>` and
  `<Outlet>`, links without a `<Link>` component, `useMatch` for active
  sections, `Register` for checked patterns, what navigation guarantees
  (`finished` after commit, scroll to top or fragment on a new page), how
  a `<ViewTransition>` animates page changes by the router's transition
  types, and how the framework reuses the navigation half.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/router` — `defineRoutes(record)` returns a table whose one operation
  is `match(pathname, accept?)` — a match `accept` declines is passed over and
  the walk goes on to the next pattern, which is how the framework skips a
  param a schema refused; `<Router routes>` mounts it on the Navigation API and
  `<Outlet />` renders the rest of the matched stack; a branch's `error`
  component (props `ErrorProps`, `{ error, reset }`; type `ErrorComponent`)
  renders in the layout's hole when what is below throws; the next
  `NavigationGeneration` clears the failure without remounting what the
  boundary wraps. `href(pattern, params?)`
  and `navigateTo(pattern, params?, options?)` build and perform navigations
  from the pattern **string** alone — no table import, so no cycle — with
  params inferred from the literal and the pattern itself checked once
  `interface Register { routes }` is augmented. `useParams(pattern)` returns
  typed params and throws if rendered under a different pattern; under the
  framework `Register` also carries `params` — the type each pattern's
  `paramsSchema` produces — so `href` takes a param as the page receives it
  (`ParsedParams` / `ParsedParamsMap` / `ParamsSchemaFor` / `ParamsOf` /
  `ErrorComponent` are the types the generated code imports); `useRoute()`
  is the untyped form.
  `@k8ordo/state`'s `Register` takes the same `routes: typeof routes`;
  `NavigablePath<typeof routes, Path>` is `Path` when a linkable pattern
  matches it segment by segment (a `:param` takes one non-empty segment)
  and `never` otherwise — a check of the path given, never a union of every
  path, which a `/:locale` page would turn into `/${string}` — for any other
  typed-path consumer. `usePathname()` reads the platform's
  pathname — never the search — so it works with or without a table, which
  makes it the location hook that also works under the framework;
  `useMatch(pattern, options?)` / `matchPath(pattern, pathname, options?)`
  answer whether that pattern — or, with a trailing `/*`, anything strictly
  below it — is the pathname showing, with its params, table-free, so a
  sidebar can ask which section is open under the framework too, and
  `{ inclusive: true }` on either counts a `/*` pattern's own index in;
  `normalizePathname(pathname)` is the router's own trailing-slash rule;
  under Vite's `base` (`import.meta.env.BASE_URL`, e.g. `/docs/`) `href` /
  `navigateTo` put it in front of every link (so `href` returns a `string`
  URL, not a table path) and `usePathname` / `<Router>` take it off, a URL
  outside it being left to the browser — `withBase(pathname, base?)` /
  `withoutBase(pathname, base?)` (`null` outside the base) are the two steps;
  `bindParams(() => ({ locale }))` returns `{ href, navigateTo }` with those
  params supplied by the source at each call (still overridable), for a
  segment every link shares — a pattern that names a param still takes
  `options` third, after an `undefined` params slot if the source supplies
  them all. `PageProps<P>` / `LayoutProps<P>` type a framework route file's
  props by its pattern (`PageProps`' `params` from the registered schemas,
  `LayoutProps`' `params` always strings and its `P` only a pattern the table
  has a page at; `request` when the generated `Register` says the mode has
  one).
  `<PathnameProvider pathname>` seeds it for a server render and hydration,
  and is mounted by `<Router>` and by both mode runtimes, never by an
  application. Every page change renders in the background, outside any
  pending async action (so awaiting `finished` inside one settles), tagged
  `navigation` and `navigation-push` / `navigation-replace` /
  `navigation-traverse` (`addTransitionType`), so a `<ViewTransition
  update={{ navigation: 'auto', default: 'none' }}>` around the pages'
  hole animates page changes and no other transition. `useInterceptedNavigation({claim, load, apply})` returns
  `{ generation }` and is the
  navigation primitive `<Router>` is built on, and the seam the framework
  uses to render server-produced trees instead; its host renders what
  `apply` set through `useDeferredValue`.
  Exported types, by group — the table: `Routes` (`{ kind, record, match }`),
  `RoutesRecord`, `RouteNode`, `RouteComponent`, `Match`, `ErrorComponent`,
  `ErrorProps`; patterns: `PatternOf`, `NavigablePatternOf`, `NavigablePath`,
  `MatchablePattern`; registration: `Register`, `RegisteredPattern`,
  `RegisteredNavigablePattern`, `RegisteredParams` (what a link takes),
  `RegisteredPageParams` (what a page receives), `PageProps`, `LayoutProps`;
  paths and schemas: `ParamsOf`, `PathFor`, `ParamValue`,
  `StandardSchemaLike`, `SchemaOutput`, `ParamsSchemaFor`, `ParsedParams`,
  `ParsedParamsMap`; options and handlers: `NavigateToOptions`
  (`{ history? }`), `MatchOptions` (`{ inclusive? }`), `BoundParams` /
  `BoundLinks` (what `bindParams`'s source returns / what it returns),
  `NavigationHandler` (`{ claim, load, apply }`).

# @k8ordo/static

> Builds a k8ordo application into files: every route rendered ahead of time,
> output a directory a static host can serve. The mode is the dependency —
> installing this package means request-time data does not exist as an API, and
> a `'use server'` module, which the RSC pipeline still compiles, is refused by
> name. `src/routes/` is the pathname space
> (page/layout/not-found/error/redirect, `[param]`, `(group)`, `_private`), a
> page or layout may `export const paramsSchema` (any Standard Schema,
> synchronous) to type its parameters — a refused value makes the pattern not
> answer, so the walk goes on to `not-found.tsx` — an `error.tsx` shows in place
> of what throws below it (in the browser; at build time a Server Component that
> throws stops the build), a `redirect.ts` is written as a page that sends the
> visitor on, a page renders its own `<title>` (React 19 hoists it), boundaries
> are React's own `'use client'` with `server-only` modules barred from the
> client bundle, and the route table and type wiring are generated rather than
> hand-written.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/static/docs/GUIDE.md): setup, the `routes/` grammar and what it refuses,
  execution boundaries, the build output, supplying pathnames for
  parameterised routes, and what static mode cannot do.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/static` — `framework(options?)` returns the Vite plugins for a
  static application (the same name `@k8ordo/server` exports, so the mode is
  the import and nothing else). `options.routesDir` moves the route directory (default
  `src/routes`); `options.paths` supplies concrete pathnames for routes with
  parameters, and a parameterised route left uncovered fails the build;
  `options.site` (the origin) makes the build also write `sitemap.xml`;
  `StaticOptions` is the type of those options. A
  `'use server'` module fails it too — in `vite dev` as well as the build: a
  file cannot receive a Server Action, so the application wants
  `@k8ordo/server` instead.

---

# @k8ordo/server

> Runs a k8ordo application: every request answered by rendering, so route
> parameters need no list of values, an unknown URL is a real 404, and a form
> can post to a Server Action. The mode is the dependency — the alternative is
> `@k8ordo/static`, which renders every route at build time. `src/routes/` is
> the pathname space (page/layout/not-found/error/redirect, `[param]`,
> `(group)`, `_private`), a page or layout may `export const paramsSchema` (any
> Standard Schema, synchronous) to type its parameters — a refused value makes
> the pattern not answer, so the walk goes on to `not-found.tsx` under a real
> 404 — an `error.tsx` shows in place of what throws below it, a `redirect.ts`
> answers 307/308, a Server Action ends with `redirect()` (303 without
> JavaScript, a navigation with it), a page receives `request` (read-only
> headers and cookies) and renders its own `<title>` — boundaries are React's
> own `'use client'` with `server-only` modules barred from the client bundle,
> and the route table and type wiring are generated rather than hand-written.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/server/docs/GUIDE.md): setup, the `routes/` grammar and what it refuses,
  execution boundaries, building and running, and what running buys over
  static.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/server` — `framework(options?)` returns the Vite plugins for an
  application that runs (the same name `@k8ordo/static` exports, so the mode
  is the import and nothing else); `options.routesDir` moves the route directory
  (default `src/routes`); `ServerOptions` is the type of `options`. This
  entry loads Vite and is for `vite.config.ts` only.
- `@k8ordo/server/runtime` — what code inside the request handler imports,
  needing nothing from Node: `redirect(to)` ends a Server Action by sending
  the visitor to `to`; `RedirectTarget` is the type of what a `redirect.ts`
  default-exports, and `RouteRequest` the type of the `request` prop.
- `@k8ordo/server/serve` — the Node.js server for a build.
  `serve({ dist?, port?, host? })` (`ServeOptions`: `dist` defaults to `dist`
  under the working directory, `port` to `3000`, `host` to `localhost`) serves
  a build and returns a `Server`, `{ port, url, close }` (`port: 0` takes a
  free port): the client build's files as they are, everything else through
  the request handler. `serve` only ever answers a request from a file inside
  the client build, whatever the pathname is spelled like.
- `dist/rsc/index.js` — the built request handler, a plain
  `(request: Request) => Promise<Response>` default export that needs nothing
  from its runtime but `AsyncLocalStorage` (`node:async_hooks`), so Node.js,
  Bun, Deno and Cloudflare Workers with `nodejs_compat` run it directly; the
  host serves `dist/client/` in front of it.

---

# @k8ordo/i18n

> The locale axis of an application, owned. `defineLocales({ ja: { timeZone,
> dir }, en: … })` declares the set once — each locale with the time zone its
> dates are shown in and its text direction — and derives membership,
> negotiation, the URL segment
> (`localize` / `delocalize`), the `[locale]` params schema in the shape
> `@k8ordo/static` / `@k8ordo/server` run, and the current locale
> (`getLocale()`). Each message is a function — `message({ ja, en })` — that
> reads the locale where it is called: on the server the request the schema
> accepted, in the browser the URL. The same call renders in a Server
> Component and in a Client Component; there is no provider and no hook; a
> bundler keeps only the messages a client module names. `Register` carries
> the app's locale union so a message missing a locale does not compile.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/i18n/docs/GUIDE.md): what the package owns and does not (the locale
  segment, not the pathname; no message grammar; no loader), the locale set
  and negotiation, messages as functions and `Register`, formatting (`Intl`
  drawn for the current locale, dates in its time zone), the Server
  Component boundary (a message is called before it is passed to a
  `'use client'` component), what reaches the browser, where the locale comes
  from on each side, `/` and `<html lang>` / `dir`, static path expansion, and
  pairing with `@k8ordo/router` / `@k8ordo/ui` / `@k8ordo/form`.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/i18n` — `defineLocales(definitions, { default? })` takes each
  locale's `{ timeZone, dir }` by tag (both required; an unknown time zone
  throws) and returns `{ all, definitions, default, is, negotiate, localize,
  delocalize, paths, paramsSchema, getLocale, run, negotiateRequest, dateTimeFormat,
  numberFormat, relativeTimeFormat, pluralRules, listFormat }`; the last five
  return the `Intl` object for the current locale, cached per locale and
  options, and `dateTimeFormat` always in that locale's `timeZone` (its
  options type refuses one); `paths(patterns)` is the static build's `paths` option
  with `/:locale` expanded to every locale; typed links come from
  `@k8ordo/router`'s `bindParams(() => ({ locale: locales.getLocale() }))`,
  written by the application; the first entry is the default unless told otherwise (and `default` is then typed as the whole union), every tag
  must be BCP 47, `negotiate(list)` tries each requested tag in order (exact,
  then language) before falling back to the default, `getLocale()` is the
  locale of the render in progress (not a hook), and `run(locale, fn)`
  (server only) runs `fn` under a locale. `negotiateRequest(request, {
  cookie? })` chooses for a `Request` — the named cookie (the visitor's
  earlier choice) first, then `Accept-Language` — through the same rule as
  `negotiate`. `parseAcceptLanguage(header)` turns an `Accept-Language`
  header into a preference list. `message(variants)`
  declares one message — text in every locale, or a function of the same
  parameters in every locale — and returns `Message<Args>`, a function that
  renders the current locale's text. Types: `Locales`, `LocaleOf`, `LocaleDefinition`, `IntlFormats`, `LocaleDateTimeFormatOptions`, `Message`,
  `Variants`, `Register`, `RegisteredLocale`, `Delocalized`,
  `LocaleParamsSchema`, `LocalesOptions`, `NegotiateRequestOptions`.

---

# @k8ordo/color-scheme

> The colour-scheme axis of an application, owned. The visitor's preference
> — light, dark, or nothing, which follows the default (the system unless
> told otherwise) — lives in localStorage through `@k8ordo/state`; one rule
> resolves it against `prefers-color-scheme`; the result is the `dark` class
> on `<html>` (what `@k8ordo/ui` reads, and Tailwind's `dark:` with a
> class-based `@custom-variant dark`). `<ColorSchemeProvider>` in the root
> layout renders the inline script that puts the class on before the first
> paint and keeps it in step afterwards; `useColorScheme()` reads it. The
> server renders the default (`light` when that default is `'system'`).
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

These docs are served from <https://ordo.k8o.me>.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](https://ordo.k8o.me/color-scheme/docs/GUIDE.md): what the package owns and does not (the class,
  not the colours; the rule, not the storage), placing the provider in the
  root layout, reading and changing the preference with the hook, what it
  guarantees, and testing.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/color-scheme` — `<ColorSchemeProvider defaultPreference?>`
  (client; goes inside `<body>` around everything) renders the inline
  `<script>` that puts `dark` on `<html>` before the first paint from the
  stored preference, the default (`'system'` unless told otherwise), or the
  system, and keeps the class in step. `useColorScheme()` returns
  `{ scheme, preference, setPreference }`: `scheme` is `'light' | 'dark'`
  on screen, `preference` is `'light' | 'dark' | 'system'`, and
  `setPreference('system')` clears the stored preference, so the default
  applies again. `colorSchemeState` is the `@k8ordo/state` local definition
  itself (`k8ordo-state:color-scheme`).
  Types: `ColorScheme`, `ColorSchemePreference`, `ColorSchemeProviderProps`,
  `UseColorScheme`.
